messages:
Olivia: hey all — onboarding question. I just migrated my dotfiles from Linux to a new MacBook (Ventura, M1). Trying to get a clean dev setup: asdf, Homebrew, node/python runtimes, ssh keys + 1Password CLI. hitting a couple weird PATH/permission things. any quick checklist?
Jamie: welcome Olivia! :wave: Quick checklist i usually run through:
  1) install Homebrew for arm: `/bin/bash -c \"$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)\"`
  2) ensure brew is on PATH: `echo 'export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zprofile` (or ~/.zshrc if you prefer)
  3) install asdf via brew: `brew install asdf` then add to shell: `echo '. $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh' >> ~/.zprofile`
  4) add plugins: `asdf plugin-add nodejs https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf-nodejs.git` and `asdf plugin-add python`
  5) install runtimes and create .tool-versions in repo root
Jamie: small gotcha: nodejs plugin sometimes needs gpg for verifying releases. `brew install gpg gnupg` before `asdf install nodejs`.
Olivia: thanks — i forgot the /opt/homebrew PATH bit, that fixed brew not found. one more: my old dotfiles had a bunch of symlinks and an rc that expects linux paths. any safe way to migrate without breaking zsh? also VSCode settings — do folks store those in dotfiles or just sync via account?
Matt: i keep VSCode settings in the account sync and only version the recommended extensions in the repo (`.vscode/extensions.json`). dotfiles: start by moving your old .zshrc -> .zshrc.local and source it from new dotfiles, then slowly migrate pieces.
Matt: ssh/1password: we use 1Password CLI for provisioning keys. make sure `eval $(op signin)` is in your onboarding steps and enable ssh-agent forwarding if you use multiple machines. also `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_rsa` helps with key persistence on mac.
Ashley: for dev tools, we recommend using direnv for per-repo env vars. install `brew install direnv` and then `echo 'eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"' >> ~/.zshrc`. put secrets in 1Password and reference non-sensitive envs in `.envrc`.
Ashley: git config: copy global name/email but avoid copying enterprise git credential helpers if they reference corp systems. `git config --global user.name "Olivia"` etc.
Olivia: nice. any Redwood-specific tips? deploy keys or shared creds to watch out for?
Jamie: check the onboarding doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/onboarding/dev-setup — follow the Private Keys section. don't commit any `.tool-versions` with secrets obviously, but do commit language versions for reproducibility.
Jamie: also, if you use zsh+oh-my-zsh: keep plugins minimal; some theme plugins slow down asdf/shims.
Olivia: OK i'll try this. will migrate dotfiles in small chunks and set up asdf + node/gpg first. thanks! :heart:
onboarding-bot: Welcome Olivia! If you want a 1:1 onboarding pairing to walk through setup, react with :raised_hands: or tag @Jamie and we'll schedule 30m.
Matt: ping me if you run into `brew doctor` warnings or permission issues, happy to jump on a call.
Olivia: will do — thanks everyone :pray:
